utah.temperature: Above normal temperatures are likely across the western CONUS as a ridge builds across the region.
utah.precipitation: Conversely, as upstream ridging gains strength across the West, below normal precipitation is favored across the northwestern quadrant of the CONUS and eastward across the Northern Plains.

ne.temperature: Near normal temperatures are now favored from the Great Lakes, Northeast, and northern Mid-Atlantic westward to the Mississippi Valley and parts of the adjacent Central and Southern Plains.
ne.precipitation: As cyclonic flow increases across the eastern CONUS, an active pattern is likely for much of the southeastern and south-central CONUS as well as for the Eastern Seaboard.

utah.temperature: As this anomalous ridge is expected to be a long duration feature, confidence is very high (greater than 80 percent) for above normal temperatures across Southern California, parts of the Great Basin, the Northern Rockies, and adjacent areas of the northern High Plains.
utah.precipitation: A slight tilt toward above normal precipitation is indicated for parts of the Southwest, tied to potential moisture advection associated with an active eastern Pacific.

ne.temperature: With increased troughing forecast, enhanced probabilities of below normal temperatures are indicated across the northeastern quadrant of the CONUS .
ne.precipitation: Above normal precipitation is favored across the Eastern Seaboard, Southeast, and eastern Gulf Coast, due to predicted cyclonic flow downstream of the western ridge .

utah.temperature: Driven by this anomalous ridging over the CONUS, the Week 3-4 Temperature Outlook indicates a tilt toward above-normal temperatures for much of western CONUS, with the highest probabilities centered over the Great Basin and southern California.
utah.precipitation: The Week 3-4 Precipitation Outlook continues to favor elevated chances of above-normal precipitation across the Desert Southwest, supported by weak troughing in the manual blend of tools.

ne.temperature: Equal Chances (EC) of above-, near-, or below-normal temperatures are forecast for the rest of the CONUS.
ne.precipitation: Conversely, ahead of the anomalous ridging, a subtle lean toward below-normal precipitation is forecast for the Northeast.

modelNote: Specifically, the GEFS depicts a broader region of positive height anomalies extending from the central CONUS to New England, whereas other dynamical models restrict these positive heights primarily to the central CONUS.
